tasks.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel, which was 1 when this was written and is 2 since round 40, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** was initially left wide on the argument that this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, share an owner, and would gain nothing from narrowing. That argument was later refused -- see the narrowing paragraph below -- and the wildcard is gone. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so the media-engine leaves these tasks genuinely share -- src/index.ts above all -- mean exactly one of this task, PL-0206 and PL-0205's successor PL-0207 can be active at a time. That was originally true of the packages/media-engine/** wildcard and it stayed true after the narrowing, because the overlap is real files rather than a wide prefix. It is a PATH fact and not a capacity one, and the distinction matters now: claude-media's maxParallel was raised from 1 to 2 in round 40, which changes nothing here because these three still share real files, and was done for PL-0601, whose surface is disjoint from all of them. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED FROM packages/media-engine/**, ON THE RULE THE REVIEWER STATED WHEN IT REFUSED PL-0205's WILDCARD: allowedPaths is write ownership, and keeping a wildcard solely because these tasks are already serialised is reservation inflation. The nine media-engine entries are the files this task actually wrote, read out of the implementation: failover.ts and scheduling.ts are the two halves of the policy, the four suites are its regressions, index.ts carries the one export line, vitest.config.ts exists ONLY for this task -- it deselects the wall-clock assertion by name so npm run check stays deterministic -- and package.json carries the ./scheduling export subpath and the bench:failover script, both created here. What is deliberately excluded is the rest of the package, which belongs to PL-0202, PL-0203 and PL-0207. ONE REVIEWDEPENDENCY ADDED, apps/web/src/components/player/playback-machine.ts. It is a CONSUMER rather than this task's work -- it imports scheduleAttempts from @liberty/media-engine/scheduling and schedules without ranking -- but the whole reason scheduling.ts exists as a separate module is that this consumer is a browser bundle edge, and failover.ts's header argues that at length. An approval that did not fingerprint the consumer would stay fresh after someone rewired it, which would silently invalidate the argument for the split. Read-only: this task does not write it, PL-0502 does. REFUSED ON THE MERITS AT 64b631d5, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A TEST WAS PROTECTING THE CLAUSE IT CONTRADICTED. boundedPolicy turned NaN into zero but deliberately left Infinity untouched, on the written argument that an infinite budget is a caller STATING a bound while only NaN is never anything a caller meant. gpt-architect refused that: an infinite budget is not a bound, it is the absence of one wearing a number's clothes. Both policy fields are ordinary numbers, so no cast is needed; attemptsUsed >= Infinity is false forever and count > Infinity is false forever, so under repeated transient failure neither the global nor the per-candidate condition ever terminates -- the unbounded reload loop pointed at a CDN that this module's own header says it exists to prevent, reached through the front door instead of through arithmetic. It directly contradicts the single acceptance clause, that retry and fallback behaviour is BOUNDED. THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING IS THE TEST. failover.test.ts pinned maxAttempts: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY as intended behaviour, with a comment restating the wrong argument. A regression suite agreeing with the code is not evidence that either is right, and this one was written to protect the clause it broke. THE FIX GENERALISES THE RULE RATHER THAN ADDING A CASE: boundedPolicy now delegates to an enforceableBudget helper that asks Number.isFinite, so the question is whether a number can bound anything at all rather than which exceptional values somebody thought of. Written as an allowlist for the same reason every other gate here is one -- NaN and the two infinities are the whole set today, but enumerating them would be a denylist over the numbers, and a denylist fails open on whatever it missed. A negative or zero budget is still passed through untouched, because that really is a caller stating a bound of nothing. Four regressions replace the one that was wrong: an infinite attempt budget, an infinite per-candidate retry budget, a NEGATIVE infinity that no enumeration of named values would have caught, and a finite budget passed through unchanged so the other three cannot pass by the guard simply zeroing everything. All three machine gates are re-recorded because the scheduler itself changed, including the bench performance gate, which the reviewer noted really had executed the timed test rather than inheriting the ordinary suite's exclusion. PROVENANCE WAS ACCEPTED, and separately the reviewer ruled on the shared introduction commit: this task and PL-0207 genuinely began in the same historical commit 4091a2b, a commit is not required to be task-atomic when recovering old history, and what matters is that the lower bound is truthful and the current review surface honest. No successor, no later base, no artificial path trimming -- record that the introduction commit is shared and leave it alone. THIS PARAGRAPH AND THE FOUR BEFORE IT SPENT TWO ROUNDS ON PL-0207'S RECORD BY MISTAKE, because the Edit anchors matched a nearly identical sentence there and neither edit was checked against the record it landed on. They are here now, and the mistake is recorded on PL-0207 rather than quietly erased. The lesson is small and general: an anchor that is unique in a diff is not necessarily unique in a file.

tasks.title: Provider health contract
tasks.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force, exit 0, 11 of 11. Also lint 0 and build 0. THE TYPECHECK IS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE HERE RATHER THAN A SIDE CONDITION, because three of the clause guarantees ARE the type and have no runtime path that could produce a wrong value: a report whose status type excludes 'pass' cannot be given one, so mutants that set status pass on the unobserved branch (M2), that put the prior score in observedSuccessRate (M4), and that add an entitlement-shaped field (M23b) fail as tsc errors -- 'src/health.ts(533,5): error TS2322' and 'error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and safeToServe does not exist in type ObservedHealthReport'. Their red is the typecheck gate, not a test file, and that is said plainly rather than dressed as a value red.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2652 passed 1 skipped (2644 before; +8, all in provider-sdk, 275 to 283). test:scripts 0, repo:validate 0. THIS ROUND CHANGED NO PRODUCTION CODE. The health mechanism was already implemented and correct in 67c5fc9 and 6c31298; what was missing was DETECTION, and a 31-mutant campaign found five places the suite would have stayed green against a wrong implementation. THE SHARPEST IS CLAUSE 5, AND IT IS A REAL HOLE THAT WAS CLOSED: the suite was strong on the mapper and BLIND ON BOTH ADAPTERS. Replacing a candidate's rights with a value chosen by the health verdict -- rights: healthReport().status === 'pass' ? 'public-domain' : source.rights -- survived all 275 tests in stremio/client.ts (M21), again for rightsBasis (M24), and again in fixture/provider.ts where the verdict is permanently unknown so the rewrite fires on EVERY candidate it produces (M25). Two reasons it was missed: nothing observed the rights VALUE at two different health verdicts, and every Stremio source in the tests was already public-domain so substituting public-domain was undetectable. Closed with a licensed source driven from warn across to pass, asserting whole-candidate equality with only healthScore overwritten: 'AssertionError: expected public-domain to be licensed'. Entitlement separation was proven three ways rather than asserted -- health.ts imports NOTHING and takes no rights, candidate or source; all three production importers were mutated in BOTH directions; and media-engine's ranking checks the rights allowlist first and unconditionally, so health can only subtract eligibility, never grant it. ALSO CLOSED: the unobserved trail could contradict its own disclaimer in a sentence beside it (M8), and policyVersion was effectively unpinned because the version enum has one member so a hardcoded string passed everything (M15, killed by a property shrunk 7 times). NO VALUE-RED WAS AVAILABLE AGAINST UNMUTATED CODE and the implementer said so rather than manufacturing one: every clause already behaved correctly at HEAD, so these tests close a detection gap rather than a behaviour gap and their red is under the planted mutant. ONE MUTANT SURVIVES AND IS DOCUMENTED IN THE TEST FILE: an optional field declared and never populated, which a name-based guard cannot see and a key-set test cannot reach because it has no runtime key; no value ever flows through it. tasks.title: Auth integration decision
tasks.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS BOTH NARROWED AND WIDENED, AND THE WIDENING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. As declared, this task reserved docs/**, apps/web/src/** and packages/contracts/** -- all twenty-one documents, the entire web application and the whole contracts package -- for a decision record. Each of those three prefix-contains an active task's write surface, so a P0 that is already finished in the tree could not be claimed by anyone. Worse, and in the opposite direction, packages/auth/** was NOT declared at all, yet nine files there are this task's primary output: a reconcile-existing run would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. Both errors come from declaring a surface by guess before the work exists rather than from reading it afterwards. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and only the control-plane record lags, the same pattern as PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0601. All four acceptance clauses are met: packages/auth exports the seam at . and ./server with better-auth a dependency of that package alone; sessions are database-backed through @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts carries ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES with findSurfaceViolations defaulting unknown plugins to violations; and both better-auth and its adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret, asserted by enabled-surface.test.ts against REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. The decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md, which self-labels Proposed because claude-lead wrote it and WAS also this task's reviewAgent when it was written -- that is no longer true, see the reviewAgent change below, and the label should be revisited by whoever closes this task. TWO HONEST CAVEATS STATED IN THE ADR RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and neither is an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed against a database, because there is no PostgreSQL anywhere in this environment; and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. PROVENANCE: this must be started with --reconcile-existing, not against HEAD. The probe is packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts -- but after the PL-0205 finding, a filename probe is not enough on its own: whoever reconciles it must confirm the candidate base tree contains neither ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES nor WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES anywhere, so a file created by a later move cannot open the range after the behaviour it claims to cover. REVIEWAGENT MOVED FROM claude-lead TO gpt-architect. This task carries a security-review gate on an authentication boundary, and its decision record was written by claude-lead. A reviewer that is also the author is not a reviewer; routing it outward makes the review stricter rather than looser, which is the only direction this may be changed in. THE MIGRATION IS A REVIEWDEPENDENCY, AND THE REVIEWER MADE THAT A CONDITION OF CLAIMING. It observed that this record cites packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql as the factual basis for the database-backed-session clause while the file sat in no part of the declared surface, and gave two defensible resolutions and one forbidden one: add it as a reviewDependency, or stop using it as evidence and let the Drizzle adapter and configuration carry the clause alone -- but do not mix the two. Its words: either is defensible; mixing the two is not. Resolved as a reviewDependency, because the ADR genuinely does rest on it: ADR-007 argues database-backed sessions over stateless ones partly on the shape of that migration, and an approval that did not fingerprint it could stay fresh after the schema underneath the argument changed. It is deliberately NOT an allowedPath -- this task did not write it, PL-0402 did, and reviewDependencies exist precisely so a boundary a task depends on can be reviewed without being reserved. No collision follows: reviewDependencies reserve nothing, so PL-0402 may still declare packages/persistence/** as a write surface whenever it is claimed.

The active profile is beside the session: active_profile_selection is its own table whose PRIMARY KEY is session_id, with foreign keys to session.id and user.id AND a COMPOSITE foreign key (profile_id, user_id) to profile (id, user_id). Scoping is in the FIRST migration rather than retrofitted: this is 0000, and playback_progress and watchlist_entry both carry a profile_id foreign key to profile in it. THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF DRIVES THE SHIPPED FUNCTIONS, not a reimplementation: createProfile, loadProfileOwnership, listProfilesForAccount, authorizeProfileSelection, selectActiveProfile, loadActiveProfileId, resolveLibertySession and archiveProfile, over a drizzle handle from the package's own createDatabase. Selection: the grant is accepted, loadActiveProfileId reads it back out of active_profile_selection, and resolveLibertySession carries it beside the session. Archive: accepted under the owner's own scope. AUTHORIZATION IS PROVEN THREE WAYS AND THE FIRST ONE WAS A HARNESS FAILURE THAT TURNED INTO EVIDENCE. Second, that decision REFUSES another account's profile as profile_not_owned_by_account, so no scope is issued at all. integration.evidence: EXECUTED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, NOT INFERRED FROM THE IN-MEMORY SUITES. PostgreSQL 16.15, a dedicated role liberty_pl0403 and its own database, migration 0000 applied to an EMPTY database (8 tables), following the PL-0402 standard. The shipped functions were driven -- issueWriterLease, writeProgress, readProgress, listContinueWatching -- over the package's own createDatabase; profiles were created through the real createProfile and scopes obtained only through authorizeProfileSelection, because issueProfileScope is not on the public surface. 12 PL-0403 assertions passed. THE (profileId, contentId) CLAUSE IS PROVEN TWO WAYS. Structurally: the PRIMARY KEY is read from pg_constraint and is exactly (profile_id, content_id), not asserted from the migration text. Behaviourally: a second write for the same key UPSERTS -- one row before, one row after, position advanced 120 to 240 and readProgress returns 240 -- and a direct INSERT of a second row for that key is refused by PostgreSQL with 23505 on playback_progress_pkey, so idempotence is enforced by the schema rather than by the repository's good manners. THE TWO-DEVICE / WRITER-EPOCH CLAUSE IS PROVEN END TO END ON THE REAL ROW. device-1 takes the lease at epoch 1 and writes. device-2 then takes the lease at epoch 2, above device-1's, which the run asserts rather than assumes. device-1's NEXT write is refused as superseded_by_newer_writer -- the classic second-device case -- AND the stored position is verified unchanged afterwards, because a refusal that still mutated the row would be the worse failure and the count alone would not have caught it. A FORGED HIGHER EPOCH, e2 + 500, is refused as epoch_not_issued: seizing authority by sending a large number does not work, which is the anti-forgery property the epoch scheme exists for and it is exercised against the real stored epoch rather than a stub. device-2, holding the current lease, then writes successfully, so the refusals are not a dead end. PROFILE SCOPING IS PROVEN ACROSS TWO REAL ACCOUNTS: a second account's profile reads null for the same contentId, and listContinueWatching returns the owner's single row and zero for the other profile -- rows are scoped to a profile id rather than a user id, which is the acceptance's first clause. ONE HARNESS DEFECT, FOUND AND CORRECTED BEFORE ANY CONCLUSION: the first run asserted `ok: true` on a write result, but ProgressWriteResolution uses `accepted` with `ok` reserved for ProgressRepositoryFailure. The failure payload showed the write had in fact succeeded with reason current_writer and notes position_first_reported and runtime_restated, so the code was correct and the assertion was not. That is the sixth harness defect this session and the pattern is reported in the handoff rather than only its instances. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: nothing about concurrency under real parallel connections -- the two devices are sequential here, which is what the epoch scheme is designed for but is not a race test -- nothing about pool behaviour under load, and nothing about migration rollback. tasks.acceptance: The machine models the session and candidate lifecycle (resolving, loading a candidate, playing, buffering, seeking, recovering, failing over, ended, fatal) rather than UI state, which the controls layer already owns; the video element and the playback engine stay authoritative and the machine is a validated projection of them, so every engine and media event has an inbound transition even in states where it supposedly cannot occur. MANDATORY CONSOLIDATION, added 2026-09-18 by gpt-architect's round-48 direction when it approved PL-0903 and PL-0904. The reviewer was explicit that these are NOT reasons to reopen either of those tasks: PL-0502 owns the whole player surface and finishes the consolidation while implementing the machine. (1) RENAME browser_unsupported to an engine-neutral lifecycle reason, host_unsupported, as a COMPLETE migration -- type member, controller, machine, tests, reason trail, docs and comments -- with NO alias kept. One lifecycle fact gets one name. Behaviour is unchanged: the engine loaded and ran far enough to determine that the current host cannot support it. (2) TIGHTEN EngineState's unavailable variant from `detail?: EngineUnavailableDetail` to `detail: EngineUnavailableDetail | null`. Every producer must state whether detail was established; omission must not be the unknown representation. This is the same required-and-nullable discipline the contracts already apply to licenseUrl and to media facts. (3) UNIFY the duplicate engine-id vocabularies. PlaybackEngineId and PlaybackErrorEngine describe the same two values. Make one authoritative and derive or alias the other in the dependency-safe direction the code comments already identify. Two independently editable literal unions for one engine identity must not remain. (4) DO NOT WEAKEN PL-0904 while integrating: never make native code/category `number | null`; do not flatten mpvError into Shaka-numbered fields; do not invent a native failure classification without evidence; keep aborted engine control flow out of candidate failure accounting. (5) PRESERVE the existing no-clock/deterministic state-machine discipline and the bounded failover policy already present in playback-machine.ts.

performance.evidence: MEASURED on e24d51f, not asserted. The repository has no bench script for apps/web, so a harness was written as a scratch vitest file inside apps/web/src/components/player/diagnostics, typechecked with npx tsc --noEmit before running (it caught nothing on the final version but DID NOT catch the first: the harness had built BufferedRange as {start,end} instead of {startSeconds,endSeconds}, which vitest surfaced as a TypeError inside describeRanges -- reported here because the rule in this project is that a harness defect is reported, not quietly fixed), run with NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc, and DELETED before commit. It is not in the tree. Five assertions, all passed, exit 0, 2.60s. CONTROL FIRST, because a timing harness with no control measures nothing: a 400-iteration sqrt loop had to cost more than 5x the cheap call. It measured 0.000739ms vs 0.000124ms, so the timer resolves differences of the size being reported. RESULTS. (1) readVideoFrameMetadata -- the function index.ts names as the one that BELONGS in requestVideoFrameCallback -- costs 0.109 microseconds per call over 500,000 steady-state iterations after a 2,000-call warmup: 0.0007% of a 60 Hz frame budget, against a declared ceiling of 1%. (2) observeAvContinuity composed with summariseAvContinuity costs 4.113 microseconds per call over 100,000 iterations, against a declared ceiling of 1ms for a telemetry tick. (3) The composed report costs 48.3x the per-frame reader. STATED PRECISELY: that ratio CORROBORATES index.ts's 'this is not a per-frame function' warning but does not by itself prove the stronger claim, because 4.113 microseconds is still only 0.025% of a 60 Hz frame in WALL CLOCK -- the header's objection is about ALLOCATION RATE (about a dozen objects per call, so roughly 700 allocations a second at 60 Hz), and allocation rate is not what a wall-clock harness measures. The ratio is the honest form of that evidence and the stronger claim is left to the header's argument. (4) THE NO-HISTORY PROPERTY, which is the one this directory's design actually rests on: 200,000 observations between two forced-gc heapUsed samples moved retained heap by -14,544 bytes -- negative, i.e. inside sampling noise and not growth. Anything genuinely retained per call would be megabytes. That is the measured form of 'nothing here holds history: no growing buffer, no ring, no subscription that outlives a session'. NOT CLAIMED: no browser-side measurement, no real media element, no requestVideoFrameCallback timing on a device. This is Node 22.22.2 on a 2-core container, and it is evidence about the pure functions' cost, which is all this module contains.

tasks.title: Search loses text typed before hydration
tasks.acceptance: Text typed into the search field before the form hydrates is not lost: on mount the form adopts the DOM value if it differs from its own state, and a query typed at any point becomes an addressable URL. Proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run on WebKit, where the race reproduces, rather than only on Chromium where it does not. Separately the spec addresses the result heading exactly rather than by substring, because role-name matching is substring by default and a query equal to a title matches both the results heading and the card heading -- a spec defect that only appeared once the suite was first executed.

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck plus npm run check, plus the standalone e2e tsc pass, exit 0 on the tree committed this round

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0, on the tree committed this round; the hydration-adoption decision is pure and tested without a DOM across nine cases including divergence, cleared-to-empty and non-hydration renders

e2e.evidence: Playwright executed in BOTH modes on 2026-09-05 at commit c47e1bba: production 78 passed / 0 failed / 18 skipped, development 87 passed / 0 failed / 9 skipped, across chromium, firefox, webkit and mobile-safari. The whole suite was green. This task's own proof, search.spec.ts 'text typed before hydration survives it', passed on all four browsers in both modes. In the previous run it was the only failure, and the cause was its own instrument rather than the product: page.unroute disposes routes without draining handlers still parked on the bundle gate, so each handler woke to find Playwright had already continued its route. It now uses unrouteAll with behavior wait. The assertions were also reordered so the address-bar check runs before the field-value check, because an UNHYDRATED field still holds what was typed into it and toHaveValue therefore passed even in the runs where React never arrived -- the URL is the only signal on this surface that cannot change without hydration, and it is the one that goes red if the adoption effect is deleted.

review.evidence: APPROVED. The hydration repair changes only the controlled field value: the layout effect does not append a search commit, advance nextEpoch, alter appliedEpoch, or mutate the request log. The first operation that can advance the epoch after adoption is the ordinary debounced commit, which records one unspent request before navigation. Reissue remains epoch-neutral and therefore cannot become adoption: an unspent matching request is classified acknowledged or stale, while an already applied matching query is classified unchanged. The executed cross-browser proof is non-vacuous now because it requires the URL to change before checking the field value, and the route instrumentation drains held handlers before removal. tasks.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. So it must be started with --reconcile-existing, never against HEAD. IT IS A MODIFICATION TASK IN THE REVIEWER'S TAXONOMY, MOSTLY, and that changes the probe. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. The precondition is a catalog source that exists in a deployment, which is PL-0305's, now READY since PL-0105 completed. ALLOWEDPATHS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. apps/web/src/app/(home)/** is DROPPED: it is a dead declaration for a route-group approach that was considered and rejected, it reserves a directory that does not exist, and it starves nothing only by accident. apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx is KEPT even though the file is deleted, because the deletion is the change and a surface that omitted it would not fingerprint the task's central act. TWO PATHS ADDED. docs/E2E.md, because it and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently CONTRADICT EACH OTHER about whether the two 404 assertions have ever been observed passing -- E2E.md claims an executed 2026-09-05 pass on all four browser projects, ci.yml says UNKNOWN, expected to pass, never observed passing -- and settling that is exactly what this task's EXECUTED clause is about. It is declared by PL-0706, which is DONE, and by PL-0703, which is BLOCKED, so no active conflict. And .github/workflows/ci.yml, which UNTIL NOW WAS DECLARED BY NO TASK IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL: every CI change this project has made has landed outside every declared surface. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.
tasks.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run ON THE PINNED BROWSER REVISION rather than by a route calling notFound(), and rather than by a run on a substituted revision. The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. THE SKELETON CLAUSE, AMENDED. Any fix must RELOCATE the loading skeletons below the existence decision rather than deleting them to move a status code, ON EVERY ROUTE WHERE A SECTION'S DATA DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE ADDRESS EXISTING. The title route is exempt, and the exemption is reasoned rather than granted: a well-formed unknown title id is indistinguishable from a real one until the catalog answers, the status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before that load resolves -- which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect this task exists to remove, so the unamended clause required the defect on one of the three routes it governs. The exemption is EMPIRICAL AND REVERSIBLE, not permanent: the moment the title page grows a section whose data does not depend on the title existing -- recommendations, continue-watching, anything PL-0301 or PL-0501 fetches separately -- it gains an in-page Suspense below the decision exactly as the watch route has, and this clause binds again. Home and watch satisfy it today and a positive check proves each, because the original wording was satisfied by a repository with no skeletons in it at all: every assertion was a not.toContain on a string that exists nowhere. tasks.title: Recommendation boundary
tasks.acceptance: The deliverable is a package and information boundary, not a recommender: eligibility is resolved upstream so recommendation can never make content playable, candidate generation may see only the active profile's explicit watchlist, that profile's progress and completion state, catalog metadata and already-resolved eligibility, and it returns content ids plus generator reasons so the reason trail survives the layer most likely to lose it

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 0ac4af8, the reconciled range bbe68ed8..HEAD. (1) npx vitest run --root packages/recommendations -> 4 files, 47 tests, exit 0 (eligibility 10, reasons 11, recommend.property 13, view 13). (2) npx turbo run test --force across the monorepo, cache-busted -> 20/20 tasks, exit 0. (3) npm run typecheck -> 21/21, own invocation, exit 0. ACCEPTANCE CHECKED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE AGAINST THE EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION, AND STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY COUNTING GREEN TESTS -- no gap was found and nothing was implemented this round. CLAUSE 1, eligibility resolved upstream: sealEligibility and resolvedEligibilitySchema mint the EligibleContentId brand; index.ts states that this package cannot mint one and only admits ids upstream already resolved as eligible. CLAUSE 2, recommendation can never make content playable: the package publishes no uri, no provider, no stream descriptor and no availability window anywhere -- grep over the non-test sources finds those words only inside comments explaining their absence -- so there is nothing in its output a player could act on even if a caller wanted it to. CLAUSE 3, candidate generation sees only the four permitted inputs: this is enforced by a TYPE, not by discipline. CandidateGenerator.generate(view: RecommendationView) takes the view and nothing else -- no profile id, no request object, no clock, no repository handle, no second parameter a later change could widen -- and RecommendationView has exactly four members, numbered in its own source: the active profile's eligible watchlist, that profile's progress and completion state, catalog metadata, and the already-resolved eligible id set. CLAUSE 4, output is content ids plus generator reasons: GeneratedCandidate is exactly {contentId: EligibleContentId, reasons: readonly [GeneratorReason, ...GeneratorReason[]]} -- a non-empty reason tuple by type, so the trail cannot be lost at the layer most likely to lose it. A FIFTH PROPERTY WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION, not required by the acceptance but load-bearing for it: no_eligibility_verdict is a separate exclusion code from upstream_not_eligible. Both exclude the work, but the first means the rights pipeline was never asked and the second means it answered no, and reporting the second as the first would tell an operator a work is unlicensed when in fact nobody asked. NO RECOMMENDER WAS BUILT and none is wanted; the acceptance says this is a package and information boundary.

THE EXACT DEFECT THIS MUST CATCH, preserved as the regression case: apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts imported @liberty/media-inspection/node/pinned-fetch while apps/web/package.json declared seven @liberty packages and not that one. It reached a reviewer because NO EXISTING GATE CAN SEE IT: the import resolves through the root workspace symlink, so typecheck, lint, build and the unit suites were green, and even npm ci --dry-run returned 0 because npm tolerates a link node that already exists. It was found by a human reader, which is not a detection mechanism. Required of the check: it reads each workspace's own manifest rather than the root's; it resolves subpath imports (@liberty/x/node/y declares @liberty/x); it covers test files as well as source, since server-bootstrap.test.ts carried the same undeclared import; and it fails the build rather than warning, because a warning in a green pipeline is how this one survived. A dry-run install against a populated node_modules does NOT satisfy this and must not be offered as the implementation. NOT IN SCOPE: the reverse direction (a declared dependency nothing imports) is a different and much weaker signal, and adding it would make the check noisy enough to be turned off. SECOND SCOPE ADDITION 2026-09-22, on gpt-architect's ruling at cd6f3efd46a75a150206617a2fa6bf747a1c3a5b: 'CI must not rely on typecheck and build racing successfully when typecheck consumes files build writes.' THE DEFECT, verified structurally rather than inferred from a flake: apps/web/tsconfig.json line 15 includes .next/types/**/*.ts; turbo.json's build task declares .next/** as an output; and turbo.json's typecheck task declares dependsOn ['^typecheck'] with NO edge to build. So tsc and next build race on that directory whenever both run in one graph. HOW IT SURFACED, because the shape of the evidence matters: a single @liberty/web#typecheck exit 2 with NO 'error TS' line in the output, which passed on two re-runs of the identical tree. The command that produced it -- npx turbo run typecheck lint build --force -- had been this project's recorded gate invocation for several rounds and had passed every time, which is what a race looks like until it does not. The lead changed its own procedure to three separate invocations, which removes the race from the evidence but NOT from CI. Required: CI must not be able to run the two concurrently in a way that lets a typecheck read a partially written .next/types. The mechanism is the implementer's -- a dependsOn edge from typecheck to build, a separate tsconfig for the check that excludes generated types, or sequencing in the workflow -- but a green run is not evidence the race is gone, so whatever is chosen must be demonstrated by argument from the task graph rather than by re-running until it passes. NOT IN SCOPE: fixing the unrelated pre-existing env:validate warnings. SMALLER AND RELATED, folded in here rather than filed: turbo.json's globalEnv lists none of the LIBERTY_CATALOG_* variables, including the eight predating round 63. Harmless today because they are read at runtime by instrumentation.ts rather than at build time, so it affects only build-cache hashing -- but a variable that is read at build time later and still unlisted would let one cache entry serve builds that meant different values, which is the defect env:validate already warns about for LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN.

tasks.title: A real catalog metadata source
tasks.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
tasks.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.

licensingDecision.decision: Wikidata is the initial catalog metadata source.
licensingDecision.rationale: It requires no credential and keeps the provider seam replaceable.
licensingDecision.scope: INITIAL SOURCE CHOICE, NOT AN EXCLUSIVE OR PERMANENT SOURCE MANDATE. Recorded in those words at the reviewer's insistence, so a later reader cannot mistake a first pick for a standard.

notCoveredByThisDecision: Any credentialed source. TMDB and anything else requiring an API key remains a separate Credentials escalation and is untouched by this.
Whether bulk ingestion engages the EU/UK sui generis database right. That question applies to Wikidata as much as to any other candidate and is for counsel, not for this record.
Commercial use terms for any future source. Only Wikidata's CC0 position on structured data was evidenced.
licensingDecision.obligationsThatFollow: Wikidata's structured data is CC0, but access is not unconditional: the Wikimedia User-Agent policy requires an informative User-Agent with contact information or the client may be IP-blocked without notice, and browser-impersonating agents are forbidden. That is why CatalogDocumentOptions.userAgent is required with no default, and it must stay that way. Text outside the main, property and lexeme namespaces is CC BY-SA rather than CC0, so the distinction has to survive into whatever is ingested.

So the deliverable is a narrowing of where the fact is asserted, not a behaviour change in routing: PROTECTION_NOT_STATED stays in PL-0501 as the fallback for every adapter that has not stated a protection fact, and this task removes the fixture from the set that needs it. tasks.acceptance: Catalog answers are served from stored ingested state refreshed on a schedule, rather than by running a full ingestion pass per query. TODAY THE ADAPTER RUNS ONE FULL runIngestionPass PER QUERY, which is correct for a seam and wrong for a deployment: it makes every page view an outbound crawl, ties response time to an upstream service, and scales the load on that service with this product's traffic. Required: the freshness and next-pass planning PL-0305 already built is what DRIVES the schedule rather than being recomputed alongside it; an answer still carries its age and stated staleness policy, so nothing becomes fresher by being cached; tombstones survive a refresh, because a work withdrawn upstream must not reappear from stored state; a refresh that fails leaves the previous state served AND SAYS SO, rather than emptying the catalog or silently serving stale data as current; and rights and availability are re-evaluated against stored records rather than trusted from the pass that stored them, since a rights basis can lapse. The reviewer noted that PL-0305 is NOT to be described as having delivered a deployed ingestion worker; this task is where that claim would become true.

tasks.title: A configured catalog with nothing usable does not look empty
tasks.acceptance: The user-facing catalog path preserves the distinction the port now makes between no_records_usable and catalog_empty. apps/web/src/lib/catalog.ts maps an empty array to 'empty' and therefore COLLAPSES THE TWO, which is the one place PL-0305's four-state work stops short of the user. The two states have different causes and different remedies: catalog_empty means the source has nothing, while no_records_usable means records exist and every one of them was withheld -- almost always for want of an operator rights basis, which is an operator action rather than a user problem. Required: catalog.ts consumes describeCatalog through requireCatalogDescription rather than inferring state from an empty array; a source that does not implement describeCatalog still works and is not reported as a failure, because the method is optional on the port by design; the user-facing copy for the withheld case does NOT promise the content is coming, since nobody has committed to obtaining those rights; and the withheld reasons are not leaked verbatim to the user, because they name internal policy vocabulary. A regression must drive both states through the real loader and observe different answers.

tasks.title: A resumed pass may not infer absence: fix what `complete` means
tasks.acceptance: `complete` means THE WHOLE SOURCE WAS OBSERVED, sufficient to infer absence -- not merely that this invocation reached end-of-enumeration. THE HAZARD, stated exactly. `IngestionPassResult.complete` is set when the provider's cursor runs out. A pass started from a non-null `resumeCursor` can reach that end having DELIBERATELY SKIPPED every page before the cursor, and it reports `complete: true`. `reconcileTombstones` takes `complete` as licence to infer absence, so every known content id living on a skipped page is unseen, is inferred withdrawn, and is mass-tombstoned. Under PL-0309's tombstone rule a tombstone is released only by a later complete pass that accepts the work again, so the damage is not self-healing on the next pass. WHY THIS IS NOT LIVE TODAY, and why that is not a reason to defer it: PL-0309's `schedule.ts` always passes `resumeCursor: null`, which keeps the hazard unreachable at the cost of re-reading the prefix every pass. The reviewer ruled it non-blocking for PL-0309 on exactly that ground and required this task BEFORE resume support is enabled. So the ordering constraint is the deliverable as much as the fix is: whoever adds resume must find this already closed. REQUIRED: absence inference is gated on a fact that a resumed pass cannot satisfy by accident. The implementer chooses the mechanism and states why -- a distinct field separating 'enumeration ended' from 'whole source observed', a fourth `TombstoneWithholdReason` for a resumed pass, or a `seenContentIds` set that makes the reconciliation exact rather than inferential. What is NOT acceptable is a comment telling a future caller not to resume, which is the state this task exists to replace. REQUIRED: a regression that fails against today's code. Start a pass from a `resumeCursor` positioned past a known id, let it run to the provider's end, and assert that id is NOT tombstoned. That test goes red on the current tree -- verify it does and say so -- which makes this a genuine red-to-green rather than a restatement. CONSIDER AND RULE ON, rather than silently skipping: `IngestionPassResult` publishes no seen set, and refusals carry native ids rather than derived content ids, so PL-0309 could not distinguish 'the complete pass saw this work and refused it' from 'never saw it' and took the conservative reading. If `seenContentIds` is the mechanism chosen here, say what it does to that narrowing. NOT IN SCOPE: enabling resume, backfill, or paging beyond `maxPages`; changing the tombstone-RELEASE rule PL-0309 delivered and the reviewer accepted; and redesigning `CatalogStore`, `applyPassToSnapshot` or `refreshCatalogIfDue`.

tasks.title: An agent instruction file has provenance, or it is not an instruction
tasks.acceptance: Repository validation detects any AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md under a working directory that is not on an explicit, reviewed allowlist, and the authoritative instruction hierarchy is stated somewhere an agent reads before it starts. THE CONCRETE CASE: apps/web/AGENTS.md is GENERATED BY next dev and instructs agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. Nothing acted on it, and it is almost certainly benign. The finding is not that file -- it is that framework tooling can write an instruction file into a directory agents treat as authoritative, which makes a dependency's postinstall a path into the control plane's instruction surface. Required: the allowlist names each legitimate instruction file and who owns it, so an unowned one is a validation failure rather than a judgement call; generated instruction files are either gitignored and removed or allowlisted after being read, and the choice is recorded per file; validation fails on an unexpected file rather than warning, because a warning in a passing run is not a control; a regression plants an unexpected AGENTS.md and observes the failure, since a detector nobody has seen fire is not known to work; and the instruction hierarchy is written down -- which file wins, and that nothing under node_modules is ever authoritative. WHAT THIS TASK MUST NOT DO: silently delete a file a framework needs, or treat allowlisting as review. An allowlisted generated file must have been READ by a human or an agent that reports what it says.

tasks.acceptance: ai:release clears implementationBaseSha, so a task returned to an unowned queue and later re-claimed records the base of the round that actually implements it. CLAUDE.md says implementationBaseSha is the exact lower bound of the first review range and that the range validator refuses a base that is either wider or narrower, so a preserved base makes the published window wider than the implementation. The rule release already follows is the argument: it discards gate results because 'evidence belongs to one implementation round under one owner', and a base is evidence of where that round began. tasks.acceptanceDisputedByImplementation: THE ACCEPTANCE ASKED FOR SOMETHING THE IMPLEMENTATION REFUSED TO BUILD, AND THE ACCEPTANCE IS LEFT STANDING RATHER THAN REWRITTEN TO MATCH WHAT WAS BUILT. I wrote 'ai:release clears implementationBaseSha'. The implementer built something else and gave the argument: the two failure directions are NOT SYMMETRIC. Always keeping the base is wrong in the PL-0710 case -- it is an unreconciled reconciliation, reaching the end state --reconcile-existing exists for while publishing none of the window, count or reason it demands. But ALWAYS CLEARING is wrong in the case PL-0710 was not: a release mid-implementation with committed work hands the next round a base at the new HEAD, so the first review range BEGINS AFTER COMMITTED CODE. A wide base is visible to a reviewer who can interrogate it; A NARROW ONE IS INVISIBLE, and narrow is the direction that lets unreviewed work reach DONE. My acceptance would have shipped a safety regression. WHAT WAS BUILT: the base survives a queue return exactly while base..HEAD still changes something under the task's REVIEWED surface -- the predicate assertReconcilableBase already relies on, not a new idea -- and where the base is kept the release event publishes preservedBaseSurfaceChangedFileCount, so preservation becomes a RECORDED FINDING rather than the silence my objection was actually about. It fails towards keeping: no git, unresolvable HEAD, base absent from the checkout or a failed diff all keep the base and name which, because dropping a published base on an unverified guess is the move this area exists to refuse. Also unlike the original ask: a task whose base was dropped can now legitimately be reconciled by the round that follows, which a released task previously never could. I ALSO FILED THIS TASK ON A FALSE PREMISE and that is recorded too: the comment at ai-control-plane.mjs:1475 documented preservation as deliberate, and I found it only after filing. It was kept and narrowed rather than deleted -- it is still true, because a reconciled base always has committed work behind it and so is never the base that gets dropped. gpt-architect should judge the delivered design against this note, not against my original clause.

review.evidence: APPROVED. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS APPROVED EVEN THOUGH IT INTENTIONALLY DOES NOT IMPLEMENT THE ORIGINAL CLAUSE, BECAUSE THE ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS UNSAFE. The reviewer's reasoning, in its own terms: implementationBaseSha is the exact lower bound of the first review range, and clearing it unconditionally after a release is safe ONLY when the abandoned round left no committed changes under the task's reviewed surface. If committed implementation work exists and the base is always cleared, the next claimant starts at the newer HEAD and the first review range begins AFTER those committed changes -- THE MORE DANGEROUS FAILURE DIRECTION, in which committed implementation can fall outside review entirely. The delivered rule is accepted in full: preserve the base when base..HEAD still changes one or more files under the reviewed surface; clear the base AND its implementationBaseProvenance when that range changes nothing there; fail conservatively toward preserving when git or history cannot establish the answer; use realHeadSha() and not LIBERTY_COMMIT_SHA for the decision; publish the decision, its reason and the changed-file count in the release and unblock audit events; apply the same rule to both commands; preserve ordinary restart semantics so start does not overwrite an existing base; and keep implementationBaseProvenance attached only while the base it explains survives. tasks.title: A superseded task needs a terminal state that is true
tasks.acceptance: A superseded task has a TRUTHFUL terminal representation, so that a provenance-invalid original whose work shipped under a named successor is neither left BLOCKED forever nor mislabelled as work nobody did. THE GAP, measured rather than asserted. control/policies.json lists eight statuses and exactly two are terminal: DONE and CANCELED. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED. There is NO cancel command on the CLI -- the reachable verbs are validate, sync, status, dispatch, claim, start, gate, review, approve, request-changes, done, block, unblock, release and event -- so CANCELED is currently reachable only by hand-editing control/tasks.json, which is the move the operating contract forbids. And scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs states at its gate-recording guard that CANCELED means 'there is no work to evidence', which is FALSE for a superseded original: the work exists, was reviewed and shipped under the successor's id. THE CONTROL PLANE ALREADY KNOWS ABOUT SUPERSESSION AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ACT ON IT. The comment at the supersession detector says a corrective re-run supersedes its predecessor and 'the predecessor is left BLOCKED deliberately -- its provenance record is preserved as audit history rather than repaired, on the rule PL-0703 established', and that BLOCKED can never reach DONE so requireAllDependenciesDone gates every dependent forever. It reports and never repairs, by design. This task does not change that: it adds a way to SAY the thing the detector already notices. REQUIRED: a terminal status that means superseded and says so -- the implementer chooses the spelling and justifies it -- carrying a REQUIRED reference to the successor task id, validated to exist and to be DONE. A status that permits a null successor is not acceptable: the whole content of the claim is which task carries the work now. REQUIRED: a control-plane command to reach it, because a terminal state reachable only by hand-editing the source of truth is worse than no terminal state. The transition must be refused when the named successor is not DONE, and the audit event must carry both ids. REQUIRED: a superseded task must NOT count as DONE in progress figures and must NOT satisfy requireAllDependenciesDone by pretending to be complete. Whether it should satisfy a dependency AT ALL is the design question and the implementer must answer it explicitly: a dependent of a superseded task is almost certainly meant to depend on the successor, and the existing detector already reports exactly that -- so the safe answer may be that supersession does NOT satisfy the dependency and the detector's advice to repoint stands. REQUIRED: the four current instances are the acceptance test, and their subsumption was audited in round 73 before this task was filed. tasks.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
tasks.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. IMPLEMENTED IN ROUND 45, AND IT IS THE ONLY TASK IN THE RECOVERY CAMPAIGN THAT NEEDED NO PROVENANCE WORK AT ALL -- genuinely unstarted, so an ordinary start captures a true base. THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL, WITH NO REGISTRY VENDORED, exactly as the script rule already is. A new spokenLanguage helper answers which language will come out of the speakers rather than which subtag a string starts with, and it differs from primarySubtag in precisely one place: where a macrolanguage has been narrowed by an extended-language subtag. BCP-47 spells a language as 2*3ALPHA optionally followed by an extlang of exactly 3ALPHA, while a region is two letters or three DIGITS and a script is four letters, so three ASCII letters immediately after a two- or three-letter primary is unambiguously an extlang and nothing else can take that shape in that position. RFC 5646 permanently invalidates the second and third extlang positions, so there is at most one to find. THE COLLAPSE RUNS TOWARD THE SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THE GENERAL, which is what makes the equivalence clause work in both directions: zh-cmn becomes cmn rather than zh, so the prefixed and bare spellings of one language agree, and the equivalence survives any region or script suffix because those subtags are never consulted. A bare zh stays zh -- it names the macrolanguage and neither variety, so treating it as either would invent a preference the viewer did not express, which is the same asymmetry the script rule uses when it says a tag naming no script conflicts with nothing. THE NEW OUTCOME IS ITS OWN REASON, as the acceptance requires: preferred_language_other_variety_only, distinct from preferred_language_other_script_only and from the regional fallback, because the three have different remedies -- a script conflict is about READING and the dialogue is still the viewer's, a regional difference is cosmetic and is still selected, and this one is the wrong language. Reporting it as a regional fallback would move the defect out of the matcher and into the vocabulary. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING THAT THE DESIGN MADE TRUE BY ACCIDENT AND THE TESTS NOW PIN: the script and variety findings are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than merely ordered. matchesOnlyAcrossScripts requires a match under ignore_script, setting the script aside leaves the spoken-language comparison, and a different variety fails it -- so zh-yue-Hant against a zh-cmn-Hans preference is not across both boundaries, it is simply the wrong language and the script question is moot. Only a track in the viewer's own spoken language can be across the script boundary, which is the only case where a font is the remedy. EXERCISED THROUGH BOTH CONSUMERS, which the acceptance demands because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift, and the way that guarantee fails is one being corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under the new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. TWO PROPERTIES HAD TO BE TIGHTENED RATHER THAN MERELY KEPT PASSING, and that is the most useful thing this task turned up. Both audio.property.test.ts and subtitles.property.test.ts asserted that a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which was a restatement of the rule being removed; once zh-cmn and cmn are both in languageTagArb it is simply false, since that is one spoken language with two primary subtags. Both now ask spokenLanguage, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher actually makes. The arbitrary gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
tasks.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

THE GENERAL LESSON, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LEARNED TWICE: the file that exists only for a task is not a safe provenance probe when a later refactor could have created that file by moving content into it. A file's creation date is the date of the FILE, not of the behaviour inside it. A probe must be chosen for when the BEHAVIOUR appeared, and the way to check that is to read the parent tree and confirm the behaviour is absent there. Eligibility must never CERTIFY an unstated codec as supported; such a candidate remains attemptable and is labelled explicitly unverified, while a STATED codec the device cannot decode is still rejected and a STATED height above the ceiling is still refused. Rights are checked before anything unknown can excuse a candidate. Scoring must neither award nor penalise a fabricated number: every unknowable dimension scores zero on a positive weight, the attainable ceiling is reported rather than used as a divisor, and nothing renormalises for what could not be measured.

tasks.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0601 and carries the same implementation forward under a base that covers the whole declared surface rather than only its code. PL-0601 recorded implementationBaseSha 33588cdce6de6a21c19a0f4725cc87b199deaa50, proven with two behaviour witnesses, liveChannelSchema and epgListingSchema, located by content pickaxe. Five checks passed and the answer was still wrong, for a reason no self-test could have caught: THE WITNESSES PROVED THE SCHEMA BOUNDARY, NOT THE TASK BOUNDARY. docs/LIVE_TV.md is an allowedPath and part of the stated implementation, and its PL-0601 rewrite -- the commit that replaced the original eleven-line Live TV note with the normalization-and-rights document -- landed at bbe68ed8d16f864c87309ceb1c089495deb89766, an ancestor of the recorded base. So the base tree already contained part of the implementation, and the published one-commit three-file window excluded task work it claimed to cover. THE TRUE BASE IS 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7, the parent of bbe68ed8, and it holds only while docs/LIVE_TV.md remains a write surface here -- which it should, because the documentation is half of what this task delivers. Claim this task, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7. PL-0601 is BLOCKED with its false narrowed base preserved as audit history; it cannot be repaired in place, on the rule PL-0703 established.
tasks.notes: MERITS ALREADY APPROVED; PROVENANCE IS THE ONLY REASON THIS TASK EXISTS. gpt-architect read the implementation at 64b631d5 and said plainly that it saw no separate architecture or rights blocker behind the provenance defect: the channel requires a real shared rights basis, EPG listings structurally cannot carry playability, strict parsing refuses injected playability keys rather than stripping them, channel and listing mismatch produces a named refusal, and the documentation describes the same boundary accurately. It declined to record either review gate, because a verdict bound to a false range is worth less than no verdict. THE SIXTH STANDING CHECK CAME OUT OF THIS FAILURE and applies to every remaining reconciliation: after a behavioural base is proposed, inspect the history of EVERY allowedPath for task-attributable work predating it. ReviewDependencies may legitimately preexist and a write surface may contain unrelated older material, but any earlier delta that is itself part of the task means the candidate base is too late. In the reviewer's words, no self-test can compensate for asking the prover only about two symbols. The practical form: for each declared write path, list the commits touching it that are ancestors of the candidate base, and refuse the base if any is attributable to this task -- the cheapest mechanical signal being the task id in the commit message, with the remainder left for inspection rather than decided by the runner. THE SWEEP REFUSED ITSELF TWICE, AND THE TWO REFUSALS MEANT DIFFERENT THINGS. The first was a bug: it read git log --oneline, which prints only the subject, while this repository writes task ids into commit BODIES, so it would have found no task id on any path and cleared every base for the wrong reason. The second, after that was fixed, was not a bug at all -- it was the check refusing a FALSE PREMISE I had built into its own positive control. I had asserted that PL-0601 must be findable in the history of docs/LIVE_TV.md, on the strength of the reviewer's sentence that bbe68ed8 replaced the original eleven-line Live TV note with the PL-0601 normalization-and-rights document. That sentence describes what the commit DID TO THE FILE. It says nothing about the commit's message, and the message is: PL-0702, close the IPv6 classifier hole and gate the rights scaffold. The Live TV document arrived as a passenger in a security commit, in the unclaimed-preflight era, and no commit touching that file has ever named PL-0601. A diagnostic round established this rather than another guess: only TWO commits have ever touched docs/LIVE_TV.md, bbe68ed8 and the repository bootstrap. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT THE MECHANICAL FORM OF THE SIXTH CHECK IS WEAK, AND IT IS WEAK EXACTLY WHERE IT WAS NEEDED. Searching pre-base commit messages for the task id would NOT have caught PL-0601's false base, because the commit carrying that task's document is labelled with a different task. The signal exists in general -- 88 commits in this history name a PL- id, and fc1ea4d names PL-0601 in its subject -- but it is absent precisely where the trap was. So the mechanical search is kept only as a cheap first filter, and the real check is now the one the reviewer's word INSPECT actually implies: the runner computes the exact set of commits reachable from the candidate base that touch ANY declared write path, and refuses unless that set matches the set recorded here as inspected. If history contains a pre-base commit nobody looked at, the reconcile does not happen. THE INSPECTED SET FOR THIS TASK IS TWO COMMITS, and both are somebody else's work rather than this task's: f06dec1b21925bf1af8c676bc7e24bc4ecf3d002, PL-AI-0006's contracts module split, which created module-boundary.test.ts; and b484735c37ce94563b346d94158437fcf1506aaa, the repository bootstrap, which created the original eleven-line docs/LIVE_TV.md. Neither is PL-0603's. domains/live.ts and live.test.ts have no pre-base history at all, because they did not exist. THE BASE ITSELF IS CONFIRMED CORRECT BY THE SAME DIAGNOSTIC: 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7 is bbe68ed8's first parent, and bbe68ed8 is NOT an ancestor of it, so the base sits before the commit that carried this task's document rather than after it. THE OLDER PARAGRAPH BELOW DESCRIBES THE FIRST REFUSAL ONLY AND IS LEFT AS WRITTEN, because it was true when it was written and the correction above is more useful than a rewrite that hides the sequence. It was built on git log --oneline, which prints only the SUBJECT line, and this repository puts task ids in commit BODIES -- the subjects are prose. So the sweep would have found no task id on any path and cleared every base for the wrong reason: a check that always passes, which is worse than no check, because it looks like one. It never got the chance, because the sweep is required to prove itself first -- PL-0601 must be findable in the history of docs/LIVE_TV.md at HEAD, where bbe68ed8 is known to have put it -- and that positive control failed, so the round reported PROBE INVALID and claimed nothing rather than reporting a refusal it had not earned. The corrected sweep reads git log's default format, which includes the full body, and adds --full-history so path-based history simplification cannot hide a commit either. The distinction between PROBE INVALID and BASE REJECTED is what made this legible instead of silent, and it was the reviewer's condition rather than my idea. SURFACE UNCHANGED FROM PL-0601, deliberately: packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts, live.test.ts, module-boundary.test.ts -- whose retired assertion that src/domains/live.ts must NOT exist is this task's edit -- and docs/LIVE_TV.md. Dropping the document to shrink the window would be reservation inflation in reverse, and it is also what made the old base look defensible. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md stays out: this task defines contracts, not HTTP routes, and the reviewer confirmed the current API document is route-oriented rather than the owner of the live-domain schema. Those routes are PL-0602's, which is BLOCKED on licensed feed access. COLLISION-CHECKED: all four entries are leaf files, prefix-disjoint in both directions from PL-0204's contracts and media-engine leaves and from PL-0405's packages/auth and docs paths.
tasks.acceptance: Licensed channel, program, schedule and EPG contracts are typed and documented. A channel carries a REQUIRED, non-nullable rights basis drawn from the one shared vocabulary rather than a restated copy. No media address may appear in a channel or a listing, and that is structural rather than conventional: a playability-bearing-key list, a compile-time witness that the listing shape carries none of them, and strict parsing so a feed sending streamUrl is REFUSED rather than silently stripped. A listing cannot yield a rights basis on its own -- resolving one requires its channel, and a listing naming another channel produces a named refusal rather than null. Ordering over listings is deterministic and total, and an offset-less timestamp is refused rather than guessed. The documentation states what the contract does not cover, including that the opaque rights reference belongs to the provider layer rather than here.
