tasks.title: Corrective, re-run: auth integration decision, with a forgeable profile scope and an unsupported pin
tasks.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0401. It carries three merits blockers as well as a provenance correction, and the merits are the larger half. PROVENANCE: PL-0401 recorded implementationBaseSha fc1ea4d54c9e7d2b2f6d9aa71a977abdc3bcb400, proven with ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES. Those witnesses correctly located the code introduction and missed earlier task implementation on another declared write path: docs/DATA_MODEL.md did not exist at 56b343 and was created in bbe68ed8, before the recorded base, already identifying itself as covering this task's auth boundary and already selecting Better Auth 1.7.1. The true lower bound is 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7 while docs/DATA_MODEL.md remains a write surface. PL-0401 is BLOCKED with the false range preserved as audit history. DO NOT CLAIM THIS TASK UNTIL THE THREE BLOCKERS IN THE NOTES ARE IMPLEMENTED; it is created now so the findings are recorded against a task rather than living only in a review transcript.
tasks.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. THE SURFACE THIS IMPLIES IS WIDER THAN THIS TASK CURRENTLY DECLARES, AND THAT IS SETTLED BEFORE THE CLAIM RATHER THAN DISCOVERED DURING IT. The reviewer offered two levels: at minimum make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability, use issuance identity as well. The minimum is NOT ACHIEVABLE IN THE TYPE SYSTEM, and PL-0706 already established why: a spread copies a branded property along with everything else and type-checks with no cast at all, so only object identity rejects it. TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable. Therefore the runtime registry is not the optional upper level here, it is the only level that works -- and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ASK. The consumers are in another package: packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts and watchlist-repository.ts read scope.profileId straight into their predicates, and profile-repository.ts and repository-scoping.test.ts also handle the type. So this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration, and it will then overlap PL-0402, PL-0403 and PL-0404, which are BACKLOG today and must be sequenced after it. The alternative -- brand and registry in packages/auth with no consumer asking -- would produce a capability that looks unforgeable and is not, which is worse than the present state because it would read as fixed. Whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. DO NOT BUMP AND LEAVE THE MIGRATION: 1.7.3 restored the 1.6 account core schema after the issuer-schema change in 1.7.0 through 1.7.2, while this repository's hand-written migration still has an issuer column and an (issuer, account_id) uniqueness rule. The migration must be regenerated or reconciled against the reviewed version BEFORE security approval. That is why packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql moves from reviewDependency to WRITE PATH here: on PL-0401 it was only evidence, and read-only was correct; here it has to change, and reviewDependencies are read-only by contract. PL-0402 also owns packages/persistence and is BACKLOG, so no active conflict exists today, but the two must be sequenced and the reviewer should say which owns that file afterwards. BLOCKER 3. ADR-007 still states obsolete control-plane routing, naming gpt-architect as preferred implementer and claude-lead as reviewer, while the record now correctly has claude-backend implementing and gpt-architect reviewing independently. Rewrite that paragraph as history rather than as current routing, and prefer wording that points at the task gate as authoritative -- otherwise completing the review needs a post-approval edit that immediately stales the fingerprint it just bound. TWO HONEST CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD FROM PL-0401, neither an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed, because no PostgreSQL exists in this environment, and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. SEQUENCING: this task is READY rather than BLOCKED because nothing external gates it, but it should not be claimed until the three blockers are implemented, and claiming it early would reserve packages/auth and two documents while no work was happening.
tasks.surfaceWidenedAtClaim: WIDENED 2026-09-15 by claude-lead in the same edit that claimed the task, which is what the notes instruct: 'this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration' and 'whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason'. TWO ENTRIES WERE ADDED, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF ADDITION. First, packages/persistence/src/**, exactly as prescribed: the registry is the only mechanism that rejects a spread forgery, TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable, and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ask, so the consumers must change. This was demonstrated rather than argued: with the issuance check in place and persistence untouched, packages/persistence/src/repository-scoping.test.ts fails six tests, because its fixtures build scopes with 'as unknown as ProfileScope' and refuseForeignScope now refuses them. progress-repository.ts moves from reviewDependency to write path for the same reason and is removed from reviewDependencies rather than listed twice. Second, package-lock.json, WHICH THE REVIEWER DID NOT NAME AND WHICH IS THEREFORE FLAGGED FOR THE REVIEWER RATHER THAN PRESENTED AS PRESCRIBED. The notes require better-auth and its Drizzle adapter to move together; the root lockfile still resolves 1.7.1, so after the pin moves, npm ci refuses the mismatch and every gate that starts from a clean install fails before it runs. Leaving it stale would ship a dependency bump that cannot be installed reproducibly, so the lockfile is part of moving the packages rather than a separate concern. It is a generated file owned by no active task; PL-0001, which generated it, is DONE. If the reviewer would rather see it as its own task, it is one entry to remove. NO OTHER WRITE SURFACE WAS ADDED, and packages/persistence/src/schema/auth.ts is inside the prescribed entry rather than an extra: it still declares the issuer column and the (issuer, account_id) unique that the migration reconciliation removes, so leaving it would make drizzle-kit propose reinstating both on the next generate. REVIEWDEPENDENCIES ALSO CHANGED, AND IT IS A REPLACEMENT RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF WRITE ACCESS. packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts left the list because it became a write path and listing it in both would say two different things about the same file. In its place the two files the reviewer named as the pattern this implementation must copy are declared read-only: packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts (ClassifiedRuntime) and packages/media-inspection/src/pin.ts (PinnedTarget). Neither is written; they are declared so the approval fingerprints the originals against which the copy is judged, which is exactly what reviewDependencies is for. If the reviewer considers that padding, they are two entries to remove and nothing else changes. SECOND WIDENING 2026-09-15, ROUND 43, BY COMMANDER INSTRUCTION AND WITH THE SAME DISCLOSURE. apps/web/src/lib/db/** was added so the in-memory repository can be converted. The first round named it as the one remaining hole and stated its bound precisely rather than reassuringly: createInMemoryRepository refuses to construct without an issued ClassifiedRuntime, so it cannot exist in a deployment -- a development- and test-process bypass, not a production one -- and it is still a cross-profile bypass, because fourteen call sites read input.scope.profileId off the object instead of asking the registry. A registry that half the repositories ask is a capability that reads as unforgeable and is not, which is the failure mode this whole corrective exists to remove, so leaving it would have been the PL-0706 defect in a THIRD place. The commander ruled on 2026-09-15 that all profile ids must flow through the same validated accessor as the production repositories. CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE ADDING: the prefix apps/web/src/lib/db is disjoint from PL-0704's apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx, apps/web/src/app/page.tsx, apps/web/src/app/title and apps/web/src/app/watch, which are the only other active apps/web declarations; PL-0701's apps/web/** would contain it, but PL-0701 is BACKLOG and unowned. Removing profileId from the ProfileScope interface entirely -- the change that turns an unchecked read from a deprecation into a compile error -- becomes reachable once this conversion lands, and whether to take it is flagged for the reviewer rather than assumed.
tasks.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range. The pinned version must be one upstream currently supports, and the hand-written migration must agree with that version's account schema rather than an abandoned intermediate one. ProfileScope must be UNFORGEABLE by a holder of a genuine scope: a spread copy carrying a replaced profileId must not remain assignable, and any consumer that grants data access on the strength of a scope must establish that the scope was ISSUED rather than merely that it type-checks. tasks.title: Supersession is a field, and a task cannot stay gated behind one
tasks.description: Four tasks -- PL-0205, PL-0401, PL-0601, PL-0703 -- are BLOCKED, terminal, and superseded by a corrective re-run. Each says so only in prose. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED, so a superseded task can never reach DONE, and with completion.requireAllDependenciesDone true, any task depending on one is gated forever. That is not a hypothetical: PL-0301 was gated behind PL-0205 while PL-0207 sat DONE, and with it PL-0302, PL-0501, PL-0502, PL-0701 and PL-0702. A human noticed. Nothing in ai:validate could have.
tasks.notes: SCOPE IS THE VALIDATOR, NOT A DEPENDENCY REWRITER. The rule reports; it never edits a dependency, because repointing a dependency is a task-definition change and those are deliberate, reasoned and recorded -- see PL-0301's own notes for what that looks like. An automatic repointer would make the graph self-modifying on the strength of a field any writer can set. THE RULE, PRECISELY. For each task T declaring supersededBy S: S must exist, must not be T, and T must not itself be DONE, or that is an ERROR, because a DONE task that claims to be superseded is two contradictory records of the same work. If S declares supersedes, it must name T -- a one-way pointer is a typo waiting to be trusted. Then, for each task D whose dependencies contain T: if S is DONE, ERROR, because D is gated behind a task that can never complete while its replacement already has; if S is not DONE, WARN, because the edge is not yet fatal but will become so the moment S completes, and a warning that arrives before the deadlock is the entire point. WHY ERROR AND NOT WARN FOR THE FIRST CASE. ai:validate already treats provenance drift as a warning and structural impossibility as an error. A dependency that can never be satisfied is structural: no sequence of legal transitions resolves it. It belongs with 'missing dependency' and 'invalid status', not with drift. WHAT THIS RULE CANNOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY OVERTRUSTS IT. supersededBy is self-asserted, exactly like fromAgent on the agent bus. It proves that somebody wrote a pointer, not that the successor genuinely carries the predecessor's work. A wrong pointer produces a wrong error or hides a real deadlock. It is a cheap alarm on a failure mode that has already cost this project one stalled milestone, not a proof of anything.
tasks.acceptance: ai:validate refuses a task graph in which a task depends on a task that declares supersededBy and whose named successor is DONE, and warns when the successor is not yet DONE. It also refuses a supersededBy naming a missing task, naming itself, declared on a DONE task, or contradicted by the successor's supersedes field. The rule reports and never edits a dependency. The four existing supersession pairs validate clean, and a regression in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs proves the rule fires -- both that it errors on a reconstructed PL-0301-behind-PL-0205 graph and that it stays silent on the repaired one, so it cannot pass by being inert.

tasks.title: Windows desktop shell and the PlayerAdapter boundary
tasks.description: Project Liberty's first production target is Windows desktop on the commander's own machine. The commander has settled the direction: a Tauri shell, the existing Next.js application preserved rather than rewritten and served by a Next standalone sidecar, a PlayerAdapter boundary the application and domain layers depend on instead of any concrete player, libmpv for compatible non-DRM playback, Shaka/EME retained for DRM-capable playback, capability routing made explicit before playback rather than discovered during it, and an LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline of our own rather than a GPL prebuilt. This task records that decision and specifies the boundary. It writes documentation only -- no shell, no adapter, no dependency is added here, because the instruction is that architecture is recorded before a large irreversible implementation, not after it.
tasks.notes: THE AUDIT CAME FIRST AND IT FOUND A CLEAN SLATE. A repository-wide search for electron, tauri, mpv, libmpv, webview2, neutralino and nw.js across every .ts, .tsx, .json, .md, .mjs and .yml outside node_modules returned nothing. So neither shell was favoured by anything already in the tree, and the decision was made on evidence rather than on inertia. Today's player is shaka-player ~5.2.6 with xstate ^5.32.5 and custom-media-element in apps/web. THE DECIDING FACT IS COMPOSITING, NOT BUNDLE SIZE. Putting HTML chrome over a hardware-accelerated native video surface in one window on Windows is a documented, shipping arrangement on WebView2 -- ICoreWebView2Controller2::put_DefaultBackgroundColor accepts alpha 0 or 255 only, and at 0 the host's content renders beneath -- and has no supported path on Chromium, where PPAPI is gone and child HWNDs are no longer in the window hierarchy. Stremio ships the WebView2 plus libmpv --wid arrangement in production on Windows and measured its previous render-API-into-a-texture approach as 2-5x worse. Any size-based argument for Tauri should be dropped: with a Node sidecar the installer lands near Electron's anyway. THE SIDECAR IS WHAT PRESERVES THE APPLICATION. Tauri's default is a static export, which would force every /api/v1 route handler off Next -- a rewrite of the application's architecture, which the instruction forbids. output: standalone in a sidecar keeps Server Components, route handlers, proxy.ts, cookies(), headers(), Server Actions and ISR working. It costs a Node runtime in the bundle, a loopback listener, supervision code and Tauri's CSP injection, which does not reach an external http origin. ONE QUESTION THIS TASK DOES NOT DECIDE AND MUST NOT DECIDE SILENTLY. A sidecar runs the application's server on a machine the user administers. If provider resolution runs there, then the boundary that enforces invariants 1 and 2 executes from files the user can read and replace, with whatever credentials it needs in its environment. The alternative is that the desktop build implements those specific routes as an authenticated proxy to the backend -- same route, same contract, same URL, a different implementation behind it, selected by build target, which is ordinary adapter work rather than a rewrite. This document states the question, states the recommendation, and leaves the ruling to the reviewer and the commander. It is a design input to PL-0501 and is cheaper to supply now than to retrofit. DRM IS A ROUTING CONSTRAINT, NOT A GAP TO CLOSE. mpv has no CDM and cannot be given one. That is not something to work around: the mpv adapter must REFUSE a DRM-protected candidate with a named reason and must never attempt it, never fall back and never degrade. Which means capability routing has to be an explicit, reasoned decision before playback -- canPlay returning a reason on both branches -- rather than a guess discovered at load time. That is what makes invariant 2 structural here rather than a promise, and it is why the boundary carries a capability descriptor at all. THE LICENSING WORK IS THE LONG POLE AND IT GATES SHIPPING RATHER THAN PROTOTYPING. A stock prebuilt libmpv is a GPL build and must not ship in a closed-source product; the one LGPL variant on offer statically links an LGPLv3 FFmpeg and carries its builder's own no-warranty disclaimer. Building our own with -Dgpl=false and an LGPL FFmpeg, with an SBOM, converts an open-ended exposure into a reviewable artifact. Nothing in this document is legal advice and counsel review is named as a precondition of shipping rather than assumed.
tasks.acceptance: A recorded architecture decision states the Windows desktop target, the Tauri shell, the preserved Next.js application served by a standalone sidecar, and the LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline, each with the evidence it rests on and the strongest argument against it. It specifies PlayerAdapter as an interface the application and domain layers depend on -- load an authorized playback session, play, pause, seek, stop, select audio track, select subtitle track, set volume, expose position and duration, expose buffering and stall events, expose recoverable and fatal errors, expose track metadata, expose A/V sync telemetry where available, dispose -- with no mpv, Electron, Tauri or Shaka type reachable from it, and names the two implementations behind it and the explicit capability routing that chooses between them, including the requirement that the mpv adapter refuse DRM-protected candidates with a named reason rather than attempt them. It states that media addresses continue to come only from authorized provider resolution and the playback-session boundary and that the client can never submit one, that stream candidate ranking stays in @liberty/media-engine, and that provider-specific logic stays in @liberty/provider-sdk. It states where provider resolution runs in the desktop build as an open question with a recommendation rather than deciding it silently, because that answer is a design input to PL-0501. It records what was verified, what was not, and which specific facts would reverse each decision. No shell, adapter or dependency is implemented here.

tasks.title: DRM capability on the candidate and playback-session contract
tasks.description: packages/contracts/src contains no occurrence of drm, widevine, playready or eme -- verified by grep across the whole source tree on 2026-09-15. So a resolved candidate carries no statement about whether it is encrypted, under which system, or against which license server. PL-0901 makes that a blocking gap rather than a cosmetic one: the desktop build routes between an mpv adapter that has no CDM and cannot be given one, and a Shaka/EME adapter that has one, and PlayerAdapter.canPlay is required to return a REASON on both branches rather than a boolean guess. A reasoned decision cannot be made from a contract that carries no field to reason about, so this gates the capability routing in PL-0901 section 4.
tasks.notes: THE SHAPE IS A CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR, NOT A BOOLEAN. An isDrm flag would answer the routing question and nothing else; the adapter also has to say WHY it refused, and a reason trail that says drm_required with no system named is not debuggable, which is invariant 4. The reviewer should expect at minimum the protection system and, where the boundary knows it, the license acquisition endpoint -- and should rule on whether an UNKNOWN encryption state is representable, because absent is not the same as none. A candidate whose encryption state was never established must not read as clear; that is the same required-and-nullable discipline PL-0207 established for media facts, and the precedent is deliberate. WHERE IT LIVES IS PART OF THE QUESTION. The descriptor could sit on streamCandidate, on the playback-session response, or on both with one deriving from the other. The candidate is what the ranker scores and the session is what the player is handed, and PL-0301's implementation already argues at packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/provider.ts that the playable address belongs on the session rather than the candidate, for a reason that may or may not extend to the key system. Settle it before writing it. NOTHING HERE MAY WEAKEN A PROTECTION. This task describes encryption so the correct player is chosen and so a refusal is explainable. It adds no decryption, no key handling and no fallback that would attempt a protected source with an engine that has no CDM -- invariant 2 -- and the mpv adapter's refusal must stay a refusal rather than becoming a degraded attempt. SEQUENCING: overlaps PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 on packages/contracts and must be sequenced after whichever is active. It should land before PL-0501 writes the session response, because retrofitting a discriminated field into a shipped contract is the change PL-0501's own acceptance warns about.
tasks.acceptance: A resolved stream candidate, or the playback session that carries it, states its content-protection requirement explicitly: the protection system where one applies, an unencrypted state that is asserted rather than inferred from an absent field, and an UNKNOWN state that is representable and does not read as unencrypted. PlayerAdapter.canPlay can decide routing from the contract alone, without inspecting a URL, a manifest or a provider-specific field, and can name the protection system in its refusal reason. Adding the field changes no existing candidate's meaning by accident: a candidate that omits it is refused by the schema rather than defaulted to clear. Provider-specific spellings stay inside @liberty/provider-sdk and are normalized before they reach the contract. No decryption, key handling or protection bypass is added.

tasks.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
tasks.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
tasks.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
tasks.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

tasks.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
tasks.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
tasks.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
tasks.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. A native error can be represented without borrowing a Shaka code and without discarding the detail the engine did supply. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.

tasks.title: A repo guard that times out under load is a guard nobody can read
tasks.acceptance: packages/media-inspection/src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts:396, the test named “is not restated by any file outside this package”, stops being a test whose result depends on machine load and on what is on disk, WITHOUT weakening the property it asserts. THE DEFECT, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN NAMED. Its failure mode is 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms', not an assertion failure -- the assertion has never reported a false offender; the test simply does not finish. Its listSourceFiles recurses into every directory under packages/ and apps/ with NO exclusions and reads every .ts file it finds: 3,680 files totalling 24.3 MB on the tree measured, of which 3,337 are under node_modules and the rest include build output. The set of files the property is actually about is 327, reachable in 1-2 ms once node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist and coverage are skipped. It is the only test in this repository whose runtime is a function of installed dependencies and build artifacts rather than of source, which is why it presents as intermittent: every other repo-walking guard here -- packages/net-policy/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/contracts/src/module-boundary.test.ts, packages/provider-sdk/src/stremio/net-policy-boundary.test.ts and apps/web/src/app/watch/route-loading-boundaries.test.ts -- is scoped to its own SRC_DIR or APP_DIRECTORY. THE REPRODUCTION GRADIENT, measured on 2026-09-22 at e24d51f on a 2-core container: the test body alone, idle with a warm page cache, 109 ms; the whole file in an isolated vitest run, 687 ms; the file under turbo run test --force with a warm cache, 849-995 ms; the same under turbo run test --force immediately after dropping the page cache, 3,048 ms. The observed failure happened on a run started immediately after the e2e suite had rewritten apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop -- thousands of freshly written files, a cold cache, background flushing, and up to nine other workspace vitest processes competing for two cores -- which is where that gradient crosses the 5,000 ms default testTimeout. REQUIRED: the walk must not descend into node_modules, .next, .turbo, dist or coverage, and the exclusion list must be stated with its reason rather than left as a magic array. REQUIRED: the property must not be narrowed to buy the speed -- it must still see every source file under packages/ and apps/ outside this package, and the implementer must show that a planted offender is still caught. A RAISED testTimeout IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE FIX ON ITS OWN: it moves the ceiling without removing the dependence on disk state, and the next person to add a dependency moves the runtime again. SECOND DEFECT, FOUND WHILE DIAGNOSING AND IN SCOPE: build output ALREADY contains the string this test looks for. Seven files under apps/web/.next and apps/web/dist/desktop carry a reference-path fragment naming m3u8-parser.d.ts inside bundled chunks. They are .js today so the .ts filter misses them, which means the test is one bundler-output change away from naming a build artifact as an offender and failing for a reason that has nothing to do with any source file. The exclusion above fixes the correctness hazard and the performance one with the same edit, which is the argument for doing it that way rather than by raising a timeout.

The cause is that the test reads 24.3 MB it has no reason to read, so its runtime tracks page-cache state and build-artifact volume, and contention only decides which side of the 5 s ceiling that lands on. unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 7423255 under the exact conditions that previously produced the failure, not under easier ones. (1) THE FILE: npx vitest run src/net-policy-boundary.test.ts in packages/media-inspection -> 23 tests (was 21; two added), exit 0. (2) THE PACKAGE: npx vitest run -> 11 files, 254 tests, exit 0. (3) THE WHOLE MONOREPO, CACHE-BUSTED AND CACHE-COLD: sync; drop_caches; npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 tasks successful, exit 0, with net-policy-boundary.test.ts at 187ms. That is the same shape as the run that timed out: turbo concurrency on 2 cores, no turbo cache, and a cold page cache. BEFORE AND AFTER, measured rather than asserted. The whole file under turbo --force with a cold page cache: 3,048ms before, 187ms after. The raw scan in isolation: 11,570ms cold unexcluded (well past the 5,000ms testTimeout that produced the observed failure) versus 15ms excluded. File count 3,680 -> 327; bytes read 24.3 MB -> 4.3 MB. The single test in isolation, cold page cache: 42ms. THE PROPERTY WAS NOT NARROWED TO BUY THAT, and two new assertions are the evidence rather than the claim. tasks.title: The application serves itself on loopback, hardened, as a standalone sidecar
tasks.acceptance: The desktop target builds a Next standalone server that a shell can spawn, and every control docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 7 names is implemented and tested. REQUIRED: output 'standalone' is set for the desktop target and only for it -- the document specifies it in two places and next.config.ts sets it in none, which is the single largest gap between the recorded design and the code. REQUIRED: the server binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly and never 0.0.0.0, asserted by a test rather than by configuration alone, because Next reads HOSTNAME from the environment and an inherited value would silently expose the listener to the LAN. REQUIRED: a per-launch 256-bit CSPRNG bearer token passed through the environment, required on every request, with a constant-time comparison and a refusal that does not state whether the token was absent or wrong. REQUIRED: Host header validation against the exact expected literal, because a bearer token does not stop DNS rebinding. REQUIRED: the application emits its own Content-Security-Policy, because Tauri's CSP injection stops applying the moment the frontend is a URL rather than bundled assets -- this is a real loss the document names and nothing currently replaces it. REQUIRED: the sidecar reports its actually-bound port on stdout rather than being told which port to use; a pick-then-bind handshake is a TOCTOU race and is refused. NOT IN SCOPE: the Rust shell, which is PW-0102.

Specifically: an absent token is refused (any local process can reach a loopback port -- there is no OS boundary between a game launcher and this server); a valid token on a rebound Host is refused (DNS rebinding makes the VICTIM'S browser issue the request, so it already holds the token and only the Host check fires); a Host differing only in port is refused (that is another listener); an EMPTY token still ARMS the guard rather than disarming it, because readSidecarEnvironment uses Object.hasOwn and not truthiness, and an empty string is a deliberate value elsewhere in this repository; and all three refusals are asserted to be BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the wire cannot be used as an oracle telling an attacker which control it had already satisfied. tasks.title: Capability routing decides the engine before playback, with a reason on both branches
tasks.acceptance: Which engine plays a candidate is decided before playback and recorded with a reason, satisfying the architecture invariant that already states this. REQUIRED: the routing function is PURE and deterministic -- no clocks, no I/O, no ambient state -- on the same rule ADR-003 and ADR-005 apply to ranking, so a routing decision can be reconstructed from a bug report. REQUIRED: a candidate whose contentProtection requires a CDM routes to the web adapter, always, and the native adapter REFUSES it with drm_required_no_cdm rather than falling back or degrading. mpv has no CDM; a native path that tried would be the DRM circumvention CONTENT_RIGHTS.md forbids, so this refusal is a rights property and not a capability detail -- which is why this task carries a rights-review gate. REQUIRED: the reason is recorded on the accepting branch as well, so 'why is this playing natively' is answerable. REQUIRED: routing consumes the protection state already on the session contract (PL-0902) rather than re-deriving it, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree. THE CANDIDATE-PROJECTION FINDING FROM PW-0201 IS THIS TASK'S, per gpt-architect's round-81 ruling, and no separate follow-up is filed unless this task proves one is needed. PW-0201 could not implement `canPlay(candidate: PlaybackCandidate)` as docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md §3 writes it: that client type is `{ id, providerId, source }`, it predates PL-0902, and it carries neither `protection` nor `compatibility` -- so an adapter handed one is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of returning `drm_required_no_cdm`, which is the refusal this task exists to make. The boundary therefore declares a narrow adapter-facing projection, and that projection is ACCEPTED. REQUIRED HERE: routing consumes the protection state from the playback-session CONTRACT -- the `protection` field `playbackSessionCandidateSchema` already publishes, which PL-0902 put there -- and never re-derives it; the adapter capability input is that narrow projection and nothing wider; NO SECOND DRM OR PROTECTION DECISION IS INVENTED anywhere in the routing path, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree and the reason trail would then explain a decision nobody made; and the native refusal `drm_required_no_cdm` remains STRUCTURAL rather than conditional. DO NOT change the adapter back to the older type to match the §3 prose: the prose was written on 2026-09-15 and PL-0902 landed after it, so the listing is stale and the code is right. A cross-package contract change is only to be proposed if this task PROVES one is required, with the specific field and the specific decision that cannot be made without it.

The rights basis of the approval, in the reviewer's own accepted terms: unknown protection is fail-closed and requires a CDM, so an unestablished encryption state can never be read as clear; the native adapter structurally refuses protected and unknown candidates under drm_required_no_cdm rather than attempting them; a protected candidate reaches Shaka only BY that refusal, which stays in the reason trail, so there is no fallback path whose purpose could be to keep trying until something plays; the 300-run property test establishes that no candidate field can disable the refusal; and no licence URL or token reaches a reason trail. tasks.title: Artwork, end to end, because a media application without images is a list
tasks.acceptance: Titles have artwork, and getting it does not become a new way to fetch arbitrary URLs. ACCEPTANCE RECONCILED IN ROUND 83 ON gpt-architect's RULING. The previous wording asked for a rights basis and dimensions 'beside the URL'. The repository already has a reviewed artwork vocabulary that deliberately carries NO URL: artworkRefSchema in packages/catalog-ingestion/src/record.ts holds a role, an assetRef constrained to an opaque lower-case token, and a REQUIRED rights basis -- required there and nowhere else in that package, on the stated argument that a work with an undeclared basis is merely refused from browse while an IMAGE with an undeclared basis that reached a page would be somebody else's file served from our origin. project.ts then drops artwork on the way to CatalogItem, and domains/catalog.ts opens by promising the browse shape carries no stream, URL or provider field. The ruling is explicit: do not weaken a previously rights- and security-reviewed opaque-reference boundary to satisfy stale task prose. REQUIRED: the catalog and title contracts carry an OPAQUE ARTWORK REFERENCE plus required display metadata and a rights basis. Not a URL. The vocabulary ADOPTS artworkRefSchema's shape rather than inventing a second one; where the two must differ, say why in the module. REQUIRED: the client never receives an arbitrary upstream image URL merely to render artwork. REQUIRED: an authorized artwork-resolution boundary turns the opaque reference into a fetchable or served asset under allowlisted transport policy. That boundary is where an origin is decided, and it is the only place one is. REQUIRED: no arbitrary URL proxy. SECURITY.md's 'never proxy arbitrary client-provided URLs' is not weakened for pictures, which is why this task carries a security review as well as a rights review. REQUIRED: absent artwork keeps the DESIGNED gradient fallback. An absent image is a designed state, not a broken one, and a broken-image icon is not the answer. REQUIRED: next/image -- or whatever equivalent configuration the implementation uses -- permits only the controlled Liberty artwork origin or boundary, never arbitrary remote hosts and never a wildcard. Because no other origin is expressible through the resolution boundary, this should be a structural fact rather than a check somebody has to remember to maintain; state which of the two the implementation achieves. MEASURED STARTING POINT, unchanged and still true: there are zero images in this product at any layer -- no next/image, no img tag, and no poster, artwork, backdrop or thumbnail key anywhere in packages/contracts/src. Posters are CSS gradients.
tasks.notes: Acceptance reconciled in round 83 on gpt-architect's ruling after a round-83 audit found the original wording would have put a URL into the one contract whose header promises there is none, and would have stood a second artwork vocabulary beside the reviewed opaque-reference one in @liberty/catalog-ingestion. The reviewer ruled: do not claim under the old acceptance, preserve the opaque-reference architecture, and resolve the reference behind an authorized boundary. An architecture-review gate was added because the task now introduces a resolution boundary rather than a field.

THREE LINT FINDINGS WERE FIXED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED, and one of them was a real defect: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect flagged the picker's initial load, and the fix was not a disable comment but rewriting the effect as an async closure with a live flag -- the component previously had no unmount guard at all, so a viewer who navigated away before the list resolved would have had setState called on an unmounted component. unit.evidence: EXECUTED on ead34dc. cd apps/web && npx vitest run over the three new suites -> avatar 15, profiles-client 20, profile-ui 14, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, with apps/web at 63 files / 1075 tests, up from 1026 last round, and every other package unchanged. WHAT THE 49 TESTS ARE FOR, BY THE PROPERTY THEY DEFEND. NO CLIENT-HELD SCOPE, WHICH IS THE SECURITY CORE: listProfiles is asserted to send no body, no query and no id, and the URL is asserted not to contain a question mark -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and a ?profileId= on a read is exactly how it comes back. selectProfile is asserted to be the only function that sends an id, to send it in the body of the selection route and never in the path or a query, and to pass a malformed id straight through rather than pre-judging it, because isMintedProfileId is the single authority and a second pattern here would answer request_malformed where the first answers profile_unavailable -- itself a small oracle. A source scan over all three modules asserts none of them reads localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie, useSearchParams, URLSearchParams or window.location, so there is no client-side source of a profile id anywhere in the directory. NOTHING UNEXPECTED REACHES THE DOM: four tests cover the unreadable path, including that an HTML error page, a script tag and a token-bearing JSON body all produce a detail containing none of their bytes -- only the zod issue PATHS and the HTTP status. A REFUSAL IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE: a 403 refused body and a 503 unavailable body both classify as answered with their reason trail intact, because collapsing them would throw away the only thing the viewer or support can act on. THE ORDER IS THE SERVER'S: three profiles served in a deliberately non-alphabetical, non-chronological order come back in exactly that order, and a source rule forbids .sort, .reverse, .toSorted and .toReversed in the picker, because oldest-first is stated in profilesResponseSchema as a promise about muscle memory. THE SWITCH CLAUSE IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY: the selected branch must contain await reload() and router.refresh() and must not contain activeProfileId:, so the picker cannot start agreeing with itself while the page shows another profile's rows. THE BADGE IS UNCONDITIONAL: AppShell is rendered with react-dom/server on three different pathnames, with and without a status badge, and profile-badge is present in all three -- no page passes a profile prop, so no route can opt out by forgetting one. FIRST PAINT MAKES NO CLAIM: the badge's first paint is asserted to contain no Choose profile, no Watching as and no href, and the picker's to be aria-busy with Loading profiles and no profile-tile and no no profiles yet -- an empty-household message shown while still asking is the worst thing a picker can say. AVATAR STABILITY IS A PROPERTY, NOT AN EXAMPLE: 500 seeds are asserted to stay in [0,360) and to spread across more than 200 distinct hues, renaming a profile is asserted not to change its hue, and the module is source-scanned for Date., Math.random, process.env, fetch(, globalThis and crypto. with a non-vacuity check. Initials are tested against an astral character and a combining sequence, which displayName[0] would split.

tasks.title: Routes authorize the caller, and a launch token is not a login
tasks.acceptance: Sensitive application routes authorize WHO is calling them, and possession of the desktop launch token is never mistaken for that. THE R4 FINDING, QUOTED: docs/SECURITY.md records that 'no authentication or authorization exists on any API route yet' and that 'nothing in the current code should be read as a decision that these routes are safe to leave anonymous'. Acceptable for a web demo; not for a shipped desktop application with a loopback listener. THIS TASK IS DELIBERATELY NOT PW-0101 AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. PW-0101 owns the LISTENER boundary -- loopback-only bind, per-launch bearer, Host validation, CSP, the port handshake -- which answers 'may this process talk to the sidecar at all'. This task answers 'may this caller perform this operation', and the two are different questions with different failure modes. A single machine-wide token that satisfied both would mean every process on the user's PC, and every page the webview ever loads, holds full authority over every profile. REQUIRED, each proven mechanically rather than asserted: (1) a protected route requires an authenticated account/session context and refuses without one; (2) a profile-scoped route authorizes the ACTIVE OR OWNED profile and never trusts a profile id supplied by the caller -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable ProfileScope as a cross-profile data-access bypass and this is the route-level half of that same defect; (3) a playback or session operation does not become authorized merely because the caller holds the desktop launch token, asserted by a test that presents a valid token and no account context and requires a refusal; (4) a refusal does not leak resource existence where an existing contract requires that property, so 'not yours' and 'not there' are indistinguishable on the wire; (5) loopback origin is NEVER treated as authentication -- a test must present a request from 127.0.0.1 with no credential and require a refusal, because 'it came from this machine' is the exact assumption that makes a local listener a privilege-escalation surface. REQUIRED: the authorization decision is made in ONE place and the routes call it, rather than each handler deciding -- a second opinion about who may read a profile is how the first one stops being enforced. USES THE EXISTING SEAM: packages/auth and the ProfileScope minted by PL-0405 are adopted and wrapped, not replaced.
tasks.notes: R4 OWNERSHIP, DECIDED AND REPORTED BEFORE THE WORK STARTS, as gpt-architect's round-80 ruling item 7 requires. No existing PW task owns the route-authorization seam cleanly: PW-0101 owns the listener and the ruling explicitly forbids broadening it into application auth merely because it already carries a security-review gate; PW-0401 owns authentication of the desktop forwarder's counterparty, which is a different service and a different caller; PW-0303 is a profiles UI and owns no route. So this is the 'one narrowly scoped PW security task' the ruling permits. It sits in Track 4 rather than in a seventh track, because the six tracks are approved and this is the same seam as PW-0401 seen from the other side -- who may call, rather than what the callee proves. The surface is the three profile-scoped handlers plus one authorization module, and it deliberately does not include the route.ts files or the contracts: if enforcement turns out to need them, that is a surface widening to state at review, not to pre-reserve. DEPENDENCY EDGE ON PW-0101 REMOVED, ROUND 82, AND THE REMOVAL IS THE POINT. It was written as a hard dependency to express "the listener exists first", and that is a READ relationship, not a build one: this task writes apps/web/src/lib/authorization and three handlers, none of which PW-0101 touches, and its negative proof -- a valid launch token with no account context is REFUSED -- needs only that the token concept exist to be refused, which it now does and is committed. requireAllDependenciesDone would have held this BACKLOG until PW-0101 cleared review, which is the PL-0311 deadlock shape: a false edge gating work that does not actually depend on it. apps/web/src/lib/sidecar stays in reviewDependencies, which is where the real relationship belongs.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on b07c535. npx vitest run src/lib/authorization -> 2 files, 27 tests, exit 0. Monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20, exit 0. THE FIVE PROOFS THE RULING REQUIRES, EACH AS A REFUSAL, because an authorization suite that mostly shows permitted callers being permitted proves the happy path and nothing about the boundary. (1) A protected route refuses with no account -- and a PROFILE route refuses on the account floor BEFORE the profile is examined, asserted by requiring the internal detail not to mention profile access, because evaluating the profile first would make "no such profile" observable to somebody who is not logged in. (2) The decision function takes NO profile id at all, asserted structurally against the source: there is no parameter a caller-supplied id could arrive through, which is the route-level form of the forgeable-ProfileScope bypass PL-0405 recorded. (3) THE LAUNCH TOKEN IS NOT A LOGIN, proven by the type signature rather than by a test that passes a header and checks it was ignored -- authorizeRoute is never given a Request, so it cannot consult the token even by accident, and the source is asserted to contain no bare `Request` type, no `headers`, and no `sidecar`. The behavioural half is there too: a caller that satisfied PW-0101's listener guard completely and carries no account is refused as unauthenticated. (4) All three not_permitted causes -- not owned, no ownership record, no active profile -- are BYTE-IDENTICAL on the wire, asserted as a one-element Set over wireDetail and over code, while STAYING DISTINCT in the internal detail, because hiding the difference from the operator too would make an authorization failure indistinguishable from a routing bug. 404 is refused for a profile the caller may not see, for the same reason. (5) LOOPBACK IS NEVER AUTHENTICATION: the source may not contain 127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost, x-forwarded-for or remoteAddress, with a non-vacuity assertion so the comment stripper is not eating the file. SECOND FILE, handler-authorization.test.ts, guards what the audit found ALREADY CORRECT across all three profile-scoped handlers: each resolves a request context; none reads a profile id by any of four spellings; the two data handlers authorize the ACTIVE profile via resolveActiveProfileScope; the external reason vocabulary cannot name a missing profile, asserted against the union declaration in packages/auth; and no handler mentions an address or the launch token. The profiles picker is exempt AND NAMED -- selection necessarily runs before any profile is active, which is why @liberty/auth publishes a separate selection decision. It opens with a non-vacuity check that every guarded file was actually read. TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND AND REPORTED RATHER THAN WIDENED AWAY: an assertion forbidding the word Request matched RequestAccountResolution and was narrowed by removing the known identifiers first, not by dropping the check; and an assertion bounding the external reason union by a 300-character window reached into the narrowing switch below it, where profile_not_found legitimately appears as a case -- that is the mapping working, not the leak -- and is now bounded to the declaration itself.

Authorization is centralized in one decision point; unauthenticated callers fail before profile evaluation; handlers do not trust caller-supplied profile ids; the existing ownership and ProfileScope enforcement is adopted rather than replaced; not-owned, no-record and no-active-profile stay indistinguishable on the wire while internal detail stays distinct; the launch token cannot become application authentication because authorizeRoute receives no Request or header surface; loopback cannot influence authorization; and a caller that satisfies PW-0101 without account identity is still refused. IMPORTANT RESIDUAL: this does NOT establish production user authentication -- account identity still derives from the development-header seam in a non-deployment runtime, and that must be resolved before production-sensitive desktop routes are considered authenticated. Owned by PW-0403.

tasks.title: A killed desktop dev server cannot leave a tracked file rewritten
tasks.acceptance: A desktop build or dev server cannot leave apps/web/next-env.d.ts rewritten in the working tree, under ANY termination. THE DEFECT, OBSERVED RATHER THAN PREDICTED, in round 81: the file was committed pointing at ./dist/desktop/dev/types/routes.d.ts instead of ./.next/types/routes.d.ts. Next regenerates that TRACKED file to name whichever distDir last built; the three *:desktop scripts snapshot and restore it around the child; and build-target.ts:300-342 already records that the restore happens ONLY ON NORMAL EXIT. Playwright signal-kills `next dev` when the harness finishes, so the rewrite survived, was staged by a routine `git add -A`, and was caught only by reading the diff before delivery. It typechecked locally because dist/desktop/dev happened to exist; on a fresh clone it would not have. REQUIRED: a forced termination -- SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL of the child, and the parent being killed -- cannot leave the tracked file dirty. REQUIRED: THE SOLUTION MUST NOT DEPEND ON A NORMAL-EXIT CLEANUP HOOK ALONE. A second `process.on('exit')` handler is the same mechanism that already failed and would fail the same way under SIGKILL; the implementer must choose a design that is correct when no cleanup runs at all, and justify it. Two candidates, neither mandated: make the file untracked and generated (which changes what a fresh clone must do, and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md must then say so), or make the desktop distDir's type path stable so no rewrite occurs. REQUIRED: the regression is MECHANICALLY TESTED -- a test that starts a desktop invocation, kills it without letting it clean up, and fails if the tracked file differs from HEAD. A test that only exercises normal exit reproduces nothing, because normal exit already works. REQUIRED: the fix does not weaken the build-target split; build-target.test.ts must keep passing, including its assertion that no shipped module under apps/web/src names LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET. NOT IN SCOPE: anything about product behaviour. This is a tooling defect and gpt-architect's ruling is explicit that it must not be folded into unrelated product work.
tasks.notes: Filed round 82 on gpt-architect's ruling item 4, which refused to let this stay a warning in a handoff. The scripts directory is named in allowedPaths because the three `node -e` wrappers inside apps/web/package.json are the thing that would move: JSON cannot carry a comment, which is why their reasoning currently lives in build-target.ts, and a real script file is the likeliest shape of the fix. It is not mandated -- the implementer chooses and justifies.

tasks.title: Production authentication and session resolution
tasks.acceptance: A request in a DEPLOYMENT can be identified, so that an account identity is never a typed header. This task owns the residual gpt-architect named when approving PW-0402, verbatim: PW-0402 does NOT establish production user authentication, and today a desktop build classifying as non-deployment would make the header the identity layer, with nothing currently preventing that classification. THE BOUNDARIES, WHICH THIS TASK DOES NOT MOVE. PW-0101 owns local listener authentication and hardening. PW-0402 owns authorization once an identity is known. PW-0401 owns the authenticated backend service for provider resolution. PW-0403 owns production account and session authentication and nothing else. REQUIRED: ADOPT the reviewed @liberty/auth/server Better Auth seam rather than replacing it. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts is already the only module in the repository that imports better-auth, it already refuses a surface beyond ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES, and config.ts already validates secure-cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour. This task constructs the reviewed instance from that validated config; it does not stand up a second identity system beside it. REQUIRED: expose the Next App Router auth handler and endpoints, importing better-auth/next-js in apps/web rather than in the package, which must stay buildable and testable without Next -- the boundary better-auth.ts states in its own header. REQUIRED: a deployment request resolves AccountIdentity ONLY from a verified database-backed session. resolveRequestAccount gains a real deployment-authenticated branch instead of answering authentication_not_configured. REQUIRED: development headers stay strictly confined to a minted non-deployment runtime capability. The witness discipline in apps/web/src/lib/session/account.ts is preserved exactly -- a deployment cannot obtain an identity there, cannot be issued the witness, and a manufactured one is refused rather than accepted on the strength of its type. REQUIRED: a missing, malformed, expired or revoked session CANNOT produce an AccountIdentity. Each of the four is its own test, because 'expired' and 'revoked' fail through different code paths and a suite that covers only the missing case proves the least interesting one. REQUIRED: the desktop launch token cannot substitute for a user session. This is the exact confusion PW-0402's authorizeRoute was built to prevent by never being given a Request, and authentication must not reintroduce it from the other side. REQUIRED: a loopback origin cannot substitute for a user session. Being on 127.0.0.1 is not an identity. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE authentication and is not moved into Better Auth user or session product data. active_profile_selection is keyed by session in Liberty's own store, which is what lets the television and the phone act as different profiles; folding it into the identity library's session record would couple the two and lose that. REQUIRED: PW-0402's indistinguishable authorization refusal behaviour is preserved. An unauthenticated request and a request for another household's resource must not become distinguishable because one of them now fails earlier. REQUIRED: secure cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour comes from the existing validated auth configuration rather than from new literals at the handler. REQUIRED: no credential or secret is placed in the desktop artifact or in any log. REQUIRED: docs/SECURITY.md R4 is updated to state what is then true. Its current text was corrected in round 82 to say authorization is enforced and authentication is not; leaving that in place after this task ships would be a second competing truth.
